comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C20-C26 regarding mTORC1 activation and soma enlargement. Both evaluations find the immunostaining and morphometric data compelling and well-supported with appropriate statistical analyses.

Strong agreement on claims C27-C31, C82 regarding neuronal positioning. Both highlight the key finding that PtenKO neurons show correct positioning despite enlarged soma size, demonstrating gene-specific mechanisms. Peer review explicitly emphasizes this as an intriguing finding showing that mTOR activation alone doesn't necessarily disrupt lamination.

Agreement on claims C32-C35 regarding capacitance and conductance increases. Peer review R3 encompasses broader electrophysiological findings (C32-C41, C49, C91) while OpenEval R3 focuses specifically on membrane properties. Both find the data well-supported.

Overlap on claims C36-C37, C41 regarding RMP changes. OpenEval R4 focuses on gene-specific RMP effects, while peer R3 covers broader electrophysiological phenotypes including decreased excitability. Both support the findings with appropriate acknowledgment of gene-specific differences.

Overlap on claims C38-C40, C49 regarding decreased AP firing and increased rheobase. OpenEval R5 emphasizes this as a convergent phenotype across conditions, while peer R3 integrates this with other electrophysiological findings. Both evaluations support the data.

Agreement on claims C42-C45 regarding altered firing patterns and spike doublets. OpenEval R6 provides detailed analysis of ISI data, while peer R4 acknowledges these as part of comprehensive gene-dependent changes in action potential properties. Both find the evidence supported.

Overlap on claims C46-C48 regarding gene-specific AP properties. OpenEval R7 focuses on AP kinetics, while peer R4 groups these with broader firing pattern changes. Both evaluations support the findings as demonstrating gene-specific differences.

Agreement on claims C56-C59, C74 regarding HCN4 upregulation. OpenEval R8 emphasizes the immunostaining validation and controls, while peer R5 highlights this as a common cellular mechanism across conditions with variations in magnitude. Both find the evidence compelling.

Agreement on claims C60-C66 regarding Ih currents and functional HCN4 expression. OpenEval R9 details the voltage-clamp data and gene-specific magnitudes, while peer R5 emphasizes this as a novel shared mechanism conferring excitability. Both support the findings with acknowledgment of variability.

Perfect agreement on claims C67-C70, C72-C73 regarding zatebradine blockade of Ih and HCN4 validation. Both evaluations confirm the pharmacological evidence supports HCN4 channel identity and its role in maintaining depolarized RMP.

Agreement on claims C71, C97 regarding BaCl2 blockade distinguishing Kir from HCN channels. OpenEval R11 explicitly discusses this control data, while peer R7 implicitly accepts it as supporting mechanistic detail without critique.

Strong agreement on claims C75-C80 regarding gene-specific synaptic transmission effects. OpenEval R12 details the sEPSC data, while peer R8 emphasizes this as a key finding demonstrating differential impact on excitatory synaptic activity and gene-specific mechanisms of hyperexcitability.

Strong agreement on claims C81, C111-C112 representing main conclusions. Both evaluations find the synthesis of convergent morphological/membrane phenotypes and divergent synaptic phenotypes well-supported. Peer review emphasizes the study achieves its aims with compelling evidence bridging different genetic causes.

Partial overlap on claims C83, C87 regarding PtenKO positioning mechanisms. OpenEval R14 rates these claims as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic explanations, while peer R2 supports the observation as an intriguing finding demonstrating gene-specific mechanisms without detailed critique of the mechanistic speculation.

Agreement on claims C88-C90 regarding severity differences and pathway organization. OpenEval R15 finds the explanations well-supported by citations, while peer R10 acknowledges gene-specific differences and suggests metabolic state analysis as future work rather than critiquing current findings.

Overlap on claims C50-C55, C93-C95, C98 regarding mTORC1-dependence. OpenEval R16 notes the limitation that rapamycin testing wasn't performed in all new conditions, while peer R5 accepts the extension to new gene conditions as part of the common HCN4 mechanism without raising this concern.

Minimal overlap on claim C91 regarding decreased intrinsic excitability. OpenEval R17 supports this as consistent with prior work, while peer R3 incorporates this finding within broader electrophysiological characterization without specific discussion of the paradox.

Overlap on claim C96 regarding Kir channel contribution. OpenEval R18 rates this UNCERTAIN because direct testing was only in Tsc1KO neurons, while peer R7 implicitly accepts this inference without critique as part of the mechanistic validation.

Minimal overlap on claim C101 regarding gene-specific synaptic effects. OpenEval R19 supports this as appropriately citing prior work and representing a key conclusion, while peer R8 emphasizes this as demonstrating differential impact on synaptic activity.

Agreement on claims C102-C105 regarding mTORC2 role. OpenEval R20 notes these are based on prior work and acknowledges uncertainty, while peer R11 rates this UNCERTAIN and suggests additional mTORC2 analysis would strengthen the study, indicating incomplete treatment.
